note: Keyed on (column, file) with a required reason, per db/gates/README.md. A name-keyed entry would be a stoplist. A NEW file reading an already-settled column is reported rather than inheriting the verdict, which is the point of listing files rather than columns.

adjudications.reason: Roster.get bench() in libs-shared/roster.mjs -- a model getter grouping the client roster by slot, unrelated to the league_formats.bench -> bench_slot_count and player.bench -> bench_press_reps renames that put the name in the universe.

Client vocabulary, not a row key. rosters/reducer.js reads the `bid` field of the add_restricted_free_agency_tag action creator (app/core/rosters/actions.js:162); auction-main-bid and auction-status read the auction slice, whose `bid` the reducer sets from payload.player_salary (app/core/auction/reducer.js:236).
dashboard-team-summary-salary/index.js builds { team_id, cap: r.availableCap, name } in its own selector. The teams route sends salary_cap and this component never reads it.
A plays-view column config object being round-tripped through browser storage. Unrelated to player.col -> college.

Roster.get cov() (libs-shared/roster.mjs:217) and the reserve-eligibility object selectors.js builds beside it. The name entered the universe from nfl_plays.cov -> coverage_on_target, a different concept.
selectors.js builds `values.div` as a division-keyed accumulator in the same function that reads it.
A fantasy stat key produced by libs-shared/calculate-stats-from-plays.mjs:120 (addStat(pid, "drops", 1)), not a column. The player_college_*logs.drops -> dropped_passes rename does not reach it.
A fantasy stat key produced by libs-shared/calculate-stats-from-plays.mjs:75, derived FROM nfl_plays.missed_or_broken_tackle rather than named after it.
Each confirmation dialog builds its own option list as { pname: player_map.get("short_name"), ... } a few lines above the read.

A request parameter carried on redux actions and view-request slices, plus the locally built auction_capacity object. The name entered the universe from nfl_plays.position -> player_position, which none of these read.

league_team_daily_values sends observed_at and app/core/league-team-daily-values/reducer.js:29 normalizes it to `timestamp` at the client boundary, so every downstream read is of the normalized key. selected-player-markets.js is normalized on the SERVER instead: GET /players/:pid/markets reshapes each row rather than sending it verbatim, emitting `timestamp: row.observed_at` and `year: row.season_year`, so `timestamp` is the wire key there and `observed_at` never reaches the client. NOTE this class is invisible to the gate: a rename at either boundary clears a name exactly as a knex alias-back does, and only the adjudication records it.

Redux action payloads, MUI option/filter objects, Highcharts axis callbacks (`this.value`), DOM form field reads and locally built { value } records. `value` entered the universe from config.value -> config_value and transactions.value -> player_salary; no site here reads either table. The two roster.js sites that DID read a roster player as `.value` were the real instance in this class and were repointed to player_salary rather than adjudicated.
